summary.gist: Oil's geopolitical shock is the dominant force today. Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers and a declared Red Sea blockade have pushed Brent toward $100 and WTI above $90, reigniting inflation fears and sending 10Y yields to 4.71% — their highest since January 2025. The energy supply disruption, compounded by Alphabet's massive capex hike and Tesla's margin implosion, creates a toxic cocktail for equities that favors energy longs, defense plays, and rate-sensitive shorts.

executive_summary: Markets face a triple headwind Friday: oil's geopolitical shock from Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers has pushed Brent near $100, 10Y Treasury yields have climbed to 4.71% on rising rate-hike expectations, and mega-cap tech is reeling from Alphabet's $195-205B capex guidance and Tesla's 14.5% single-day crash. S&P futures show a modest overnight bounce to 7,541 from yesterday's 7,408 close, but the risk-off tone dominates. Energy and defense names are the clear beneficiaries, while airlines and rate-sensitive equities face headwinds. AXP and NEE report today and could provide cross-currents.

macro_events.title: Houthi Red Sea Blockade and Saudi Tanker Attacks
macro_events.causal_chain: Houthis attack two Saudi tankers (Encelia and Layla) and declare full maritime embargo on Saudi ports > Bab al-Mandeb crossings drop 34% to 29 vessels > 6.2M bbl/day of oil and 20% of global LNG transit at risk > WTI jumps to $90.65 (+4.8%), Brent to $99-100 (+5.6-7%) > war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs > Asian refiners consider Cape of Good Hope reroute (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) > inflationary pressure feeds into 10Y yield rise to 4.71% > Fed rate hike probability jumps to 78% for September
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Red Sea / Bab al-Mandeb > global oil and LNG supply chains > US monetary policy
macro_events.historical_analog: September 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent spiked 15% in 24 hours, tanker rates ran 20-35% in one week. Current situation more sustained due to blockade declaration vs one-off strike.
macro_events.counterargument: Saudi Arabia has rerouting capacity via Yanbu. US CENTCOM strikes may degrade Houthi capability. Strategic petroleum reserves provide buffer.

macro_events.title: Alphabet Q2 Earnings: Cloud Surge vs Capex Shock
macro_events.causal_chain: GOOGL reports $119.8B revenue (+24% YoY), Cloud +82% to $24.8B > but capex guidance hiked to $195-205B for full year 2026 (nearly doubling from 2025) > negative free cash flow of $5.85B > investors question AI capex ROI sustainability > GOOGL drops ~7% > contagion to AI/semi complex as market re-rates capex-heavy names > NVDA, AMD, AVGO face sentiment drag despite strong AI demand fundamentals
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US tech sector > global AI infrastructure spending
macro_events.historical_analog: Meta Q3 2022 metaverse capex selloff — stock dropped 25% on capex concerns before recovering. Key question is whether GOOGL Cloud growth justifies the spend.
macro_events.counterargument: Cloud revenue growing 82% YoY may justify the investment. Search revenue +17% shows core business remains strong.

affected_tickers.reason: AI capex is demand for NVDA GPUs but market questioning sustainability

macro_events.title: Tesla Q2: Record Revenue, Margin Implosion
macro_events.causal_chain: TSLA reports $28.2B revenue (+26% YoY) on record 480K deliveries > operating income collapses 57% to $398M (1.4% margin) > EPS $0.33 vs $0.53 expected (39% miss) > FCF deficit of $1.09B > stock crashes 14.5% to $320, erasing $140B market cap > signals EV pricing war eroding margins industry-wide
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US auto sector > global EV market dynamics
macro_events.historical_analog: Tesla Q4 2022 selloff when margins compressed from price cuts — stock dropped 65% peak-to-trough. Current margin compression deeper (1.4% vs ~5% then).
macro_events.counterargument: Volume growth of 26% shows demand intact. Margin compression may be temporary as new model ramp costs normalize.

affected_tickers.reason: Massive EPS miss and margin compression
EV losses but traditional auto margins more stable

macro_events.title: Treasury Yields Hit 2025 Highs on Rate Hike Fears
macro_events.causal_chain: 10Y yield rises to 4.71% (4th consecutive session, highest since Jan 2025) > 30Y at 5.17% > oil-driven inflation expectations combine with hawkish Fed stance > markets price 33% chance of July hike, 78% for September > higher discount rates compress equity valuations > TLT falls, banks benefit from steeper curve
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy > global rates and risk assets
macro_events.historical_analog: October 2023 — 10Y hit 5.0% before Fed pivot. Current dynamic different as oil supply shock creates new inflationary impulse.
macro_events.counterargument: Fed may view oil shock as transitory supply disruption. Core PCE could remain stable if energy pass-through is limited.
